body.x: SOLVE LINE (CEO SangYoon Lee) announced its participation in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10to, as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

With extensive experience in control systems from AUTONICS and SNT Motiv, CEO Lee established SOLVE LINE to become a global leader in industrial automation, PLC programming, and smart factory solutions within five years. The company has been recognized for its innovative LabVIEW-based SCARA robot control program, developed through the 2022 preliminary startup package. It has since expanded its capabilities by establishing an in-house R&D department in 2023.

In 2024, SOLVE LINE advanced its expertise in digital transformation (DX) technologies, particularly by developing a digital twin-enabled SCARA robot control program. This innovative solution enhances factory automation and extends DX applications to industrial settings.

The company boasts a strong portfolio, including developing Alpha Robotics’ smart gripper control PC program, retrofitting Hyundai Motors’ Genesis assembly line for mixed production, and automating ultrasonic cleaning systems for LK. In 2024, SOLVE LINE secured contracts with global giants such as Samsung Heavy Industries and Bandobots, earning recognition for its technological excellence in industrial automation.

At CES 2025, SOLVE LINE will highlight its SCARA robot digital twin program, a cost-effective alternative for small and medium-sized manufacturers. Digital twin technology replicates physical factory environments in a virtual 3D space, enabling real-time visualization and interaction. The company has focused on developing an affordable yet highly capable SCARA robot solution tailored to smaller-scale enterprises that face challenges in investing in large-scale automation systems.

Electronics, automotive components, and medical devices are targeted industries where advanced manufacturing processes are crucial. The solution applies to academic research labs, government agencies, and institutions exploring new automation technologies.

A SOLVE LINE representative emphasized, “The growing adoption of smart factories has increased the demand for automation solutions. Digital twin technology, which virtually simulates physical operations, is a compelling alternative for companies seeking to avoid severe penalties under strict workplace safety laws like Korea’s Serious Accidents Punishment Act.”

The company plans to expand beyond domestic markets, targeting high-demand regions such as the U.S. and leveraging aggressive marketing strategies to establish a global presence in industrial robotics.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
